chapter: The 1920s road: dance style and management
title: Bubbles marries in Cleveland after Buck's wedding
summary: After leaving Chicago they went to Cleveland where Bubbles married a chorus girl, reasoning he would help his own wife if he could not help Buck's.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Were there any prospects for you getting married at the same time?
Sure, if I want to. But the point of it was, though, George, --
Was Buck traveling with his wife now, the three of you?
Listen. We are now in Cleveland at the time -- we were in Chicago when he gets married and we leave Chicago on account of that letter coming from New York from the manager and I go to Cleveland.
When I get to Cleveland I decided I was getting married. Do you follow me? So I get married in Cleveland -- was it Cleveland -- Ohio., I get married.
Where did she come from?
Chicago.
And how long had you been seeing her?
Where did she come from -- how do you mean?
How long had you been seeing her? She didn't seem to have been playing a part --

Look, they both were in the show. They both were in the show in the cafe. They both were in the chorus line. Both girls were in the chorus line. Understand? So I hadn't ought to get married at the time, until he got married. He knew he couldn't support his wife -- or a wife. I thought I would get married because I can't help him, I
would help my wife. This was my idea. Do you understand me or do you?
Not really.
Okay.
He got married so you felt that it was your time to get married, too?

No, no, no. I didn't feel it at that time, no, no. I went from Chicago to Cleveland before I thought about that. But if anything crops up about his wife that I have already told him and her that he can't afford it then I won't be responsible because I'm going to have the same difficulty.
That's it.
I see what you mean. What am I going to do?
Well, you're doing that you don't want to have responsibility for them.
What will I do?
You'll get married, too.
And what will that mean?
It means that you won't have responsibility towards them, you'll have responsibility towards your wife.
And anything he wants to do for his wife I've got to do for mine, you know.
That's right.
Ain't that sensible?
Right.
